🛩️ Before He Was “The Professor,” He Was Flying Combat Missions

Most people remember Russell Johnson as the calm, intelligent Professor on Gilligan’s Island.

On the show, he could fix almost anything with a little ingenuity and whatever materials happened to wash up on the island.

But long before television fame, Johnson had already lived through something far more dangerous.

During World War II, he served as a bombardier aboard a B-25 Mitchell bomber in the Pacific Theater. Between 1942 and 1945, he flew 44 combat missions against Japanese forces, taking part in the intense aerial campaigns that stretched across the Pacific.

These missions were among the most dangerous assignments of the war. B-25 crews faced anti-aircraft fire, enemy fighters, and long flights over hostile territory.

In March 1945, during one of those missions over the Philippines, Johnson’s plane was shot down.

He survived the crash, but the impact broke both of his ankles. For his injuries and service, he was awarded the Purple Heart.

Like many veterans of that era, he rarely centered his fame around his wartime experiences. To later generations, he became a beloved television character.

But behind the familiar face of “The Professor” was a man who had already faced the realities of war in the skies over the Pacific.

Sometimes the most recognizable faces from television carry stories far bigger than the roles we remember them for.

GM to those who keep grinding. Here is your daily Market Movers (03.11):

CRYPTO ROUNDUP

₿ $BTC stuck at $69.5K, couldn't hold $71K Tuesday as war uncertainty kept risk appetite in check. Fear & Greed at 25, up from last month's Extreme Fear but still firmly in Fear territory.

📊 $BTC ETFs saw $167M net inflow on Mar 9, BlackRock leading. $ETH, $XRP, $SOL ETFs all posted outflows same day, suggesting narrow institutional demand.

⚡ Strategy (fka MicroStrategy) bought 17,994 $BTC for $1.28B between Mar 2-8 at avg $70,946. Total holdings now 738,731 BTC. Saylor buying the war dip.

🔵 $DOT Polkadot spot ETF (ticker TDOT) now live on Nasdaq, with a hard catalyst March 12: a major economic upgrade cutting emissions 53.6% and capping supply.

AI & TECH

🤖 $ORCL exploded 13.8% on earnings, raised FY2027 sales guidance to $90B. Revenue $17.19B, up 18%, beat by $270M. Cloud up 41%. Management called SaaS apocalypse fears overblown, says AI agents will strengthen platforms, not cannibalize them.

🤖 Apple's rebuilt Siri targeting March 2026 release with iOS 26.4, powered by Google's Gemini 1.2T parameter model via Private Cloud Compute. The AI assistant wars are heating up.

🤖 IRGC released a list of top US companies with Israeli links whose tech has been used militarily. $NVDA, defense/AI chip supply chains on watch if list triggers secondary sanctions pressure.

FINANCE & INVESTMENT

📉 Feb CPI: +2.4% YoY, +0.3% MoM, in line with forecasts. Core CPI +2.5% YoY, unchanged from Jan. The report predates the Iran oil shock entirely, so Mar CPI will be the real test.

📉 $SPX flat to slightly positive in early trade. $ORCL rally lifted Nasdaq (+0.3%), $NVDA edging higher. $GOLD pulling back to $5,181 from $5,219 yesterday as energy fears ease slightly.

⚠️ Feb jobs report shed 92,000 jobs vs. expectations of +58,000 added. Unemployment 4.4%. Worst monthly reading since 2020. Stagflation risk rising as energy shock hits into a weakening jobs market.

🏦 Fed March 18 decision: markets pricing 100% hold. No cuts through April now consensus. Warsh confirmation as Fed Chair looming as a major variable for H2 rate trajectory.

GEOPOLITICS

🇺🇸🇮🇱🇮🇷 Day 12 of Operation Epic Fury. Hegseth called today "our most intense day of strikes yet" with the most fighters, bombers, and strikes deployed so far.

🇮🇷 Iran says nearly 10,000 civilian sites bombed, 1,300+ civilians killed. Internet blackout at 240 hours, among the longest state-imposed shutdowns on record globally.

🇮🇷🇦🇪 UAE refinery hit by Iran drone strike, fire reported. 85 countries have now reported petrol price rises since Feb 28. Manila introducing 4-day work week in response to fuel costs.

🇱🇧 Israel began ground raids into southern Lebanon, weighing deeper push. Hezbollah front reopening alongside Iran conflict. Second front expanding.
